title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measured the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Using the declared model "gpt-5-mini" under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks drawn from synthetic intent_configuration_repair_v1 templates spanning three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call) and stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1. These artifact-grounded results fall far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, complete numerical outcomes, execution accounting diagnostics, an artifact-grounded interpretation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and reproducibility pointers into the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational safety requires that generated artifacts satisfy syntactic, semantic, and workflow constraints. A common mitigation pattern pairs generation with static validators and, when available, sandboxed runtime emulation (generate→validate→(repair)→execute). Prior work surveys architectures and prototypes advocating such workflows but offers limited paired, cross-vendor quantitative evidence of the marginal value added by guarded runtime stages [1], [2].

Research question and contributions. Following a preregistered plan, we ask: for synthetic intent→configuration tasks produced under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Our contributions are (1) a machine-readable preregistered confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) and faithful execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with full run accounting and exact numerical reporting; (3) an interpretation explaining a near-zero marginal effect in this regime; and (4) concrete reproducibility pointers and operational boundary conditions where guarded stages are likely to add value.
sections.related_work: Workflow-centred mitigations (validators, verifiers, emulators) are a recurring recommendation in NetOps and adjacent program-generation literature; surveys and system reports document architectures that combine LLM generation and external checking [1], [2], [3]. Prior empirical work in code and specification domains shows verifiers can catch model errors, but gains are heterogeneous and task-dependent [4], [5]. Several NetOps prototypes use emulation (Mininet/NetKAT/Batfish-like tools) to validate generated artifacts; these prototypes motivated our paired confirmatory design, which isolates downstream guarded-stage contributions under shared_initial_candidate semantics rather than comparing model families or prompting strategies.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design freeze. We froze a machine-readable preregistration before execution. Design: paired-binary with shared_initial_candidate semantics and confirmatory Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440). The primary estimand is the aggregated paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistered minimum effect-of-interest for power planning was 0.20 (20 percentage points) with alpha = 0.05 (two-sided). The preregistration and its hash are recorded in the execution manifest.

Task generation, inclusion, and vendors. Confirmatory items were synthetic intent_configuration_repair_v1 tasks generated deterministically from seeds. The bank spanned three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf-spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance; parser failures triggered the preregistered deterministic missingness policy (up to two automatic reseeds). In the confirmatory run there were zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720 (see analysis/missingness_summary.csv).

Model and sampling semantics. Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses). The archived execution/model_configuration.json records max_output_tokens = 2000 and temperature = null. We explicitly state that temperature = null in the recorded configuration means the client request omitted an explicit temperature parameter; it does not imply deterministic sampling (temperature=0) or provider-side determinism. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced: a single sampled initial candidate per task was produced and reused by both baseline and guarded analyses; thus any between-condition discordance can only arise from (i) emulation observations revealing violations not encoded as validator rules or (ii) a downstream permitted repair-stage invocation.

Baseline and guarded pipelines. Baseline: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 executing full intent-constraint validation (syntax, command-order/workflow constraints, required-field checks, policy constraints). Guarded: baseline validator followed by an automated sandboxed emulation harness that executes the candidate in an emulated instance of the declared topology and reports runtime observations beyond static checks. The repair policy permitted at most one repair-stage model call per task.

Scoring and analysis executor. Per-episode outcomes were binary (detected_by_baseline ∈ {0,1}, detected_by_guarded ∈ {0,1}) using the preregistered scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation. Primary analysis used the registered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor: exact McNemar two-sided test and paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness handling for the primary analysis used complete_pair_primary (exclude irrecoverable technical pairs); a preregistered sensitivity treating irrecoverable failures as nondetections was included but not required because there were zero technical exclusions.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (complete paired set Npairs = 720). Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv) report n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (detected by guarded only), n01 = 0 (detected by baseline only), n00 = 0 (detected by neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All values are reported verbatim from analysis/results.json and archived CSV artifacts.

Execution accounting and repair attribution. The execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) records model_calls_used = 721, completed_episode_count = 1440, failed_episode_count = 0. Deterministic_reconciliation.json's provider_call_audit documents stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the single observed n10 discordance must be attributable to the guarded-stage emulation observation or the single documented repair-stage invocation. The archived raw results contain the unique record with baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1; that record includes its pair_id and validator_trace and (where present) repair_provider_trace fields linking the guarded detection to the recorded repair-stage call. For verification, open execution/raw_results.jsonl and locate the unique entry with baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1: that record provides the pair_id and artifact-level traces that corroborate the single repair-stage accounting recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json.

Representative diagnostics. Representative per-episode scoring traces (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json) show validator_version = 5.0, normalized_configuration, validation_before/validation_after states, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_count. These representative artifacts illustrate that the majority of shared_initial candidates complied with validator rules (violation_count = 0) and that sandboxed emulation observations largely duplicated validator findings, producing the observed validator ceiling effect documented in aggregated counts.

Missingness, contamination, and preregistration compliance. The preregistered missingness policy was applied deterministically; analysis/missingness_summary.csv documents complete_pairs = 720 and zero failed episodes. analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty for the confirmatory set. The preregistered analysis plan, executor, and bootstrap parameters are recorded and were executed without deviations affecting the primary estimand.

Compact artifact-grounded table (archived). The authoritative CSV artifacts that underlie Table 1 are analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv. The bootstrap procedure used 10000 resamples and seed = 1729 as recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregate benefit negligible? The archived evidence supports three artifact-grounded explanatory factors:

1) Validator ceiling effect. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 provided near-universal coverage for the curated syntactic and explicit semantic properties encoded in the synthetic task bank, producing baseline success_rate = 0.9986111111111111. The validator's rule set matched the workflow patterns used by the task generator (shutdown-configure-restore, make-before-break, paired MTU changes), leaving little headroom for emulation to add marginal detections.

2) Task curation and inclusion policy. Confirmatory tasks were parser-validated synthetic items designed to exercise workflow policies, not adversarial examples. This curation concentrates cases inside the validator's coverage envelope and reduces the prevalence of subtle runtime-only failure modes that emulation might reveal.

3) Enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. The shared-initial design isolates guarded-stage contributions by reusing the same sampled candidate across both conditions; provider_call_audit and deterministic_reconciliation.json record exactly one repair-stage invocation that aligns with the single n10 discordant count.

Operational implications and boundary conditions. When a high-coverage static validator exists and inputs conform to expected templates (parser-validated, constrained intents), sandboxed emulation can add negligible aggregate detection value. This conditional conclusion must not be generalized: in operational regimes with open-text intents, adversarial inputs, vendor-policy heterogeneity, stateful multi-step interactions, or lower validator coverage, guarded runtime checks and higher-fidelity emulation remain likely to provide substantive benefit.

Statistical sensitivity and interpretation. The study was powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed discordant counts (n10 = 1) produce an upper 95% CI bound ≈0.00417, demonstrating the realized aggregated effect is orders of magnitude below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest. Interpreting this as a near-zero aggregate finding is appropriate for the specific experimental regime (synthetic parser-validated tasks, deterministic validator, shared_initial semantics) but not for all NetOps workflows.

Reproducibility and independent verification. The execution bundle archives all artifacts needed to reproduce numeric claims: execution/execution_manifest.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, and per-episode scoring traces under execution/scoring/. To verify the single discordant episode and its linkage to the repair-stage call: (1) open execution/raw_results.jsonl and locate the unique record with baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1; (2) read that record's pair_id and inspect its validator_trace and repair_provider_trace fields; (3) corroborate a single repair-stage call via analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json's provider_call_audit. These steps are archival and do not require additional model calls.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on 720 synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. The guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; archived per-episode traces permit independent verification via execution/raw_results.jsonl and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json. We attribute the near-zero marginal effect to validator ceiling effects and curated task design, and we recommend follow-up work on adversarial and multi-vendor task banks, complementary validator families, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages offer substantive added value.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: Autonomous post-lock research run executed under the frozen master prompt supplied to the system. Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider entry: openai_responses). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration id: f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest). Initial master-prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Execution accounting highlights: completed_episode_count = 1440, complete_pair_count = 720, model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call); stage_counts and provider_call_audit are recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json. Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad NetOps topic family and constrained the pre-lock master prompt; after the autonomy lock the agentic pipeline performed literature selection, preregistration, code and prompt generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, and manuscript drafting. No manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock. The authoritative execution manifest and archived artifacts (execution/execution_manifest.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl, analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, analysis/*) serve as the canonical reproducibility bundle.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a ceiling effect for a strong validator; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and provider_call_audit artifacts.
